title: Design
text: SymJ is a symbolic manipulation kernel written in pure Julia. It aims for SymEngine-class speed with a small, explicit core that later layers (simplification, solving, matrices) build on.

title: Goals
text: Speed comparable to SymEngine. Construction, canonicalization, expansion, differentiation and substitution should be within a small factor of SymEngine, and ideally faster.Callable objects. Symbolic objects subtype Function (via AbstractSymbolic). Calling is meant to make expressions drop-in …

text: lambdify(ex, x, y) compiles ex into a Julia function of x and y, in that order. Without variables, ex may have at most one free symbol. title: SymJ
text: Documentation for SymJ.

title: SymJ.SymJ
text: SymJ Symbolic manipulation with a single concrete, hash-carrying node type, eager canonicalization of sums, products and powers, exact numbers, and support for the TermInterface v2 contract. See docs/src/design.md for the design.

title: SymJ.AbstractSymbolic
text: AbstractSymbolic <: Function Supertype of SymJ's symbolic objects. Symbolic objects are callable: calling an expression substitutes into it (see subs) and calling a SymFunction builds an unevaluated function application.

Not exported. Calling …

title: SymJ.Poly
text: Poly{C} Sparse multivariate polynomial in the generators gens(p) with coefficients of type C: SymNumber for numeric coefficients, or Sym for symbolic ones. Terms are stored in lex order with gens(p)[1] most significant. Poly(ex, x, y, ...) Convert the expression ex to a polynomial in x, y, .... …

title: SymJ.Sym
text: Sym A symbolic expression. Construct leaves with Sym(:x), Sym(2), Sym(1//3), Sym(π), or the @syms macro; build compound expressions with the usual arithmetic operators and functions. Expressions are kept in a canonical form as they are built: like terms are collected in sums, like bases are …

title: SymJ.SymFunction
text:
SymFunction(name) A symbolic function. Calling it builds an unevaluated application: f = SymFunction(:f)     # or `@syms f()`
f(x, 2)                 # f(x, 2)

title: SymJ.SymInterval
text: SymInterval An interval of the real line with exact endpoints: lo, hi (nothing for -∞, ∞) and whether each end is closed. A point is the closed interval [a, a].

title: SymJ.SymNumber
text: SymNumber <: Real Numeric scalar used inside symbolic expressions. It is exact (an integer or rational of arbitrary size) unless constructed from a floating point value. Small values never allocate; arithmetic promotes to BigInt on overflow and demotes back when results fit.

title: SymJ.SymSet
text: SymSet A finite union of disjoint intervals with exact endpoints, sorted and merged; the solutions of an inequality (solve). Supports in, ∪, ∩, setdiff, isempty; the intervals are S.intervals. Calling tests membership: S(2), or S(x => 2) for a set from solve(ineq, x) (which records its variable).
